style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized. Authored in six stanza-group pieces and assembled.
chapterNote: The Bible's longest chapter: twenty-two stanzas of eight verses, one stanza per Hebrew letter, every verse an acrostic jewel about the Word of God -- and nearly every verse naming it by one of eight great titles: torah the instruction, dabar the word, imrah the spoken promise, choq the statute, mitsvah the commandment, mishpat the judgment, edut the testimony, piqqudim the precepts. It is a love song before it is a law song: the psalmist tastes the Word like honey, treasures it like plunder, sings it in the house of his pilgrimage, rises before dawn and wakes through the night watches for it, and counts affliction good because it taught him the statutes. The famous verses are famous rightly -- hidden in my heart (v. 11), a lamp to my feet (v. 105), the entrance of Your words gives light (v. 130), before I was afflicted I went astray (v. 67) -- but the psalm's genius is its whole arc, sustained affection across an entire alphabet, ending in the humblest place possible: I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant. The man who loved the law longest knew best that only the Shepherd's seeking would bring him home.

1.text: ALEPH. Oh the blessedness of those whose way is whole and blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD.
1.amp: ALEPH. Blessed [esher] are the undefiled ['perfect, sincere', tamim, the KJV margin -- whole, blameless] in the way [derek], who walk [halak] in the law [torah -- the instruction] of the LORD [YHWH].
1.notes: The great acrostic opens like Psalm 1, with esher (H835), blessedness -- and its first word for Scripture, torah (H8451), instruction wider than statute. tamim (H8549) is wholeness of way: integrity as a road walked, not a score kept.

2.text: Oh the blessedness of those who guard His testimonies, who seek Him with the whole heart.
2.amp: Blessed [esher] are they that keep [natsar -- guard as a watchman] His testimonies [edah], and that seek [darash] Him with the whole heart [leb].
2.notes: The second beatitude joins the book's two great pursuits in one clause: natsar (H5341) His edot (H5713), the covenant testimonies -- and darash (H1875) HIM. The Word is kept in order to seek its Author; all 176 verses run on that distinction.

3.text: They practice no injustice at all; they walk in His ways.
3.amp: They also do [paal -- work, practice] no iniquity [avlah -- injustice]: they walk [halak] in His ways [derek].
3.notes: paal (H6466) is settled practice, not a stray slip: the blessed do not make avlah (H5766) their trade. The walking-verb halak carries the whole psalm -- obedience as locomotion, a direction more than a moment.

4.text: You Yourself have commanded Your precepts, that we keep them with all diligence.
4.amp: You have commanded [tsavah] us to keep [shamar] Your precepts [piqqudim] diligently [meod -- exceedingly].
4.notes: piqqudim (H6490), the precepts -- the overseer's appointed charges, Scripture-word number four -- and the standard is meod (H3966), exceedingly: diligence proportioned to the Commander, not to convenience.

5.text: Oh that my ways were set firm to keep Your statutes!
5.amp: O that [achalay -- would that!] my ways [derek] were directed [kun -- established, made firm] to keep [shamar] Your statutes [choq]!
5.notes: achalay (H305), the longing particle: the psalmist's first personal word is a sigh at the gap between verse 1's blessed way and his own. kun (H3559) asks for fixedness -- ways that hold their heading.

6.text: Then I would not be put to shame, when I look steadily at all Your commandments.
6.amp: Then shall I not be ashamed [bosh], when I have respect [nabat -- look steadily] unto all [kol] Your commandments [mitsvah].
6.notes: Shame's cure is a steady gaze: nabat (H5027) at KOL the mitsvot (H4687) -- the whole counsel, not a favorites list. Selective obedience always leaves an exposed flank; bosh (H954) finds the commandment we skipped.

7.text: I will give You thanks with an upright heart, as I learn the judgments of Your righteousness.
7.amp: I will praise [yadah] You with uprightness [yosher] of heart [lebab], when I shall have learned [lamad] Your righteous judgments ['judgments of thy righteousness', mishpat tsedek, the KJV margin].
7.notes: lamad (H3925), the learning-verb: praise deepens as the syllabus advances -- thanksgiving is the sound a student makes. The mishpatim (H4941) are His judicial rulings, Scripture-word six, each one a window into tsedek (H6664).

8.text: I will keep Your statutes; do not forsake me, not ever, not utterly.
8.amp: I will keep [shamar] Your statutes [choq]: O forsake [azab] me not utterly [meod].
8.notes: The Aleph stanza closes with resolve and dependence in one breath: I will shamar -- and do not azab (H5800) me, for the resolve cannot outlive Your presence. Every vow in this psalm leans on the God it is made to.

9.text: BETH. How shall a young man keep his path clean? By guarding it according to Your word.
9.amp: BETH. Wherewithal shall a young man [naar] cleanse [zakah -- keep pure] his way [orach]? by taking heed [shamar] thereto according to Your word [dabar].
9.notes: The question every generation asks, answered in one clause: the naar (H5288) stays zakah (H2135) by ruling his orach (H734) with the dabar (H1697). Not willpower, not environment -- alignment with the Word.

10.text: With my whole heart I have sought You; do not let me stray from Your commandments.
10.amp: With my whole heart [leb] have I sought [darash] You: O let me not wander [shagah -- stray, err] from Your commandments [mitsvah].
10.notes: The whole-heart seeking of verse 2 in the first person -- and immediately the fear of drift: shagah (H7686), the unintentional wander. The seeker knows his own feet; he asks to be kept, not merely informed.

11.text: Your word I have treasured up and hidden in my heart, so that I might not sin against You.
11.amp: Your word [imrah] have I hid [tsaphan -- treasured up, stored] in my heart [leb], that I might not sin [chata] against You.
11.notes: The memory verse of memory verses: imrah (H565), the spoken word, tsaphan (H6845) -- stored like treasure in the vault where temptation makes its offers. Sin is fought at the heart's counter, and the stocked heart wins.

12.text: Blessed are You, O LORD; teach Your statutes to me.
12.amp: Blessed [barak] are You, O LORD [YHWH]: teach [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
12.notes: The psalm's shortest theology: worship first -- barak (H1288), blessing God Himself -- then the request that recurs more than any other in the psalm: lamad, teach me. The blessed God is the wanted Teacher.

13.text: With my lips I have recounted all the judgments of Your mouth.
13.amp: With my lips [saphah] have I declared [saphar -- recounted, tallied] all the judgments [mishpat] of Your mouth [peh].
13.notes: saphar (H5608), the recounting-verb of Psalm 22:22: what the heart stored (v. 11) the saphah (H8193) now spends. From His peh to my lips -- Scripture's intended round trip.

14.text: In the way of Your testimonies I have rejoiced, as over all riches.
14.amp: I have rejoiced [sus] in the way [derek] of Your testimonies [eduth], as much as in all riches [hon].
14.notes: The wealth-comparison begins (it will escalate to thousands of gold and silver in v. 72): joy in the edut (H5715) weighed against hon (H1952), the whole portfolio -- and found equal. The psalmist audits his gladness and likes the books.

15.text: On Your precepts I will meditate and muse, and keep my gaze on Your paths.
15.amp: I will meditate [siach -- muse, turn over aloud] in Your precepts [piqqudim], and have respect [nabat -- gaze] unto Your ways [orach].
15.notes: siach (H7878) is rumination with the lips moving -- the psalm's counterpart to Psalm 1's hagah. Meditation here has an object and an outcome: the piqqudim turned over until the orach comes into focus.

16.text: In Your statutes I will delight myself; I will not forget Your word.
16.amp: I will delight [shaa] myself in Your statutes [chuqqah]: I will not forget [shakach] Your word [dabar].
16.notes: shaa (H8173): delight as deliberate self-entertainment -- the psalmist plays in the statutes. And delight is memory's best keeper: what the heart enjoys, shakach (H7911) cannot easily take.

17.text: GIMEL. Deal in full bounty with Your servant, that I may live, and I will keep Your word.
17.amp: GIMEL. Deal bountifully [gamal] with Your servant [ebed], that I may live [chayah], and keep [shamar] Your word [dabar].
17.notes: gamal (H1580), to deal out fully: the servant asks wages he has not earned, for a purpose he cannot fake -- life spent on obedience. chayah (H2421), the psalm's revive-verb, makes its first appearance; it will carry the whole song.

18.text: Unveil my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your law.
18.amp: Open ['Reveal', galah, the KJV margin -- unveil] my eyes [ayin], that I may behold [nabat] wondrous things [pala] out of Your law [torah].
18.notes: galah (H1540) is the unveiling-verb of revelation itself: the pala (H6381), the wonders, are already IN the torah -- the request is for eyes. The prayer to pray before every reading of Scripture (cf. Luke 24:31-32, 45).

19.text: I am a sojourner on the earth; do not hide Your commandments from me.
19.amp: I am a stranger [ger -- a resident alien, a sojourner] in the earth [eretz]: hide [satar] not Your commandments [mitsvah] from me.
19.notes: ger (H1616): the legal term for the resident alien -- on earth without citizenship papers (cf. Hebrews 11:13; 1 Peter 2:11). A stranger needs the local Sovereign's law disclosed; the mitsvot are the immigrant's handbook for the country he is passing through.

20.text: My soul is crushed with longing for Your judgments at every moment.
20.amp: My soul [nephesh] breaks [garas -- is crushed] for the longing [taabah] that it has unto Your judgments [mishpat] at all times [et].
20.notes: garas (H1638), crushed to pieces -- by desire, not affliction: appetite for the mishpatim at load-bearing intensity, be-kol-et, at every time. The psalm's affections run this hot throughout; the doctrine never cools it.

21.text: You have rebuked the insolent proud, the accursed, who stray from Your commandments.
21.amp: You have rebuked [gaar] the proud [zed -- the insolent] that are cursed [arar], which do err [shagah -- stray] from Your commandments [mitsvah].
21.notes: The zedim (H2086), the high-handed proud of Psalm 19:13, stand under God's own gaar (H1605), His rebuke. Straying (shagah) that hardens into pride ends under arar (H779) -- the psalm's warnings are as serious as its delights.

22.text: Roll reproach and contempt away from me, for I have guarded Your testimonies.
22.amp: Remove ['roll', galal, the KJV margin] from me reproach [cherpah] and contempt [buz]; for I have kept [natsar] Your testimonies [edah].
22.notes: galal (H1556), roll it off -- reproach as a boulder on the back. cherpah and buz (H2781, H937): the sneer obedience draws in a crooked generation; the psalmist asks God, not the mockers, to take it away.

23.text: Though princes sit in session and speak against me, Your servant muses on Your statutes.
23.amp: Princes [sar] also did sit [yashab] and speak [dabar] against me: but Your servant [ebed] did meditate [siach] in Your statutes [choq].
23.notes: The sarim (H8269) convene -- official opposition, a bench of it -- and the ebed answers with counter-programming: siach (H7878) in the choq. He cannot control the council chamber; he can control what his mind chews.

24.text: Yes, Your testimonies are my delight; they are the men of my counsel.
24.amp: Your testimonies [edah] also are my delight [shaashuim] and my counsellors ['men of my counsel', anshe atsati, the KJV margin].
24.notes: Against the princes' committee (v. 23) the psalmist seats his own: the edot as anshe etsah (H6098), the men of his counsel -- Scripture as a cabinet of advisors that outvotes any court. shaashuim (H8191), delight: the advisors he actually enjoys.

25.text: DALETH. My soul lies clinging to the dust; revive me according to Your word.
25.amp: DALETH. My soul [nephesh] cleaves [dabaq -- clings fast] unto the dust [afar]: quicken [chayah -- revive] me according to Your word [dabar].
25.notes: dabaq (H1692), the covenant cleaving-verb, tragically misapplied: the nephesh stuck to afar (H6083), the dust of Genesis 3:19 -- flattened, at death's doorsill. The remedy is the psalm's great refrain-request: chayah (H2421), revive me, ki-dbarekha, on the strength of Your word.

26.text: I laid out my ways before You, and You answered me; teach me Your statutes.
26.amp: I have declared [saphar -- recounted] my ways [derek], and You heard [anah -- answered] me: teach [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
26.notes: saphar again -- but now the psalmist recounts his OWN ways, confession's full inventory, and anah (H6030): God answered. The forgiven man's next request is always the same in this psalm: lamad, teach me.

27.text: Make me understand the way of Your precepts, and I will muse on Your wondrous works.
27.amp: Make me to understand [bin] the way [derek] of Your precepts [piqqudim]: so shall I talk [siach -- meditate, muse] of Your wondrous works [pala].
27.notes: bin (H995), discernment: not more information but the WAY of the precepts -- how they run, where they lead. Understanding overflows as siach on the pala (H6381), the wonders; taught men become tellers.

28.text: My soul weeps itself away for heaviness; raise me up and strengthen me according to Your word.
28.amp: My soul [nephesh] melts ['droppeth', dalaph, the KJV margin -- drips away in tears] for heaviness [tugah -- sorrow]: strengthen [qum -- raise up, establish] me according unto Your word [dabar].
28.notes: dalaph (H1811), the leaking-roof verb of Ecclesiastes 10:18: the soul dripping away tear by tear under tugah. The asked strength is qum (H6965) -- to be stood back up -- and the specified means is the same as verse 25's: according to Your word.

29.text: Remove the way of falsehood far from me, and be gracious to me with Your law.
29.amp: Remove [sur] from me the way [derek] of lying [sheqer -- falsehood, deception]: and grant me Your law [torah] graciously [chanan].
29.notes: Two ways lie before every man in this stanza: the derek sheqer (H8267) and the derek emunah of the next verse. The striking phrase is torah given by chanan (H2603), by grace -- law itself received as gift, not burden.

30.text: I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I have set Your judgments before my eyes.
30.amp: I have chosen [bachar] the way [derek] of truth [emunah -- faithfulness]: Your judgments [mishpat] have I laid [shavah -- set level] before me.
30.notes: bachar (H977): the deliberate election every disciple makes -- the derek emunah (H530) over the derek sheqer. shavah (H7737) is to set level in view: the mishpatim arranged on the dashboard where the eyes actually rest.

31.text: I cling to Your testimonies, O LORD; do not let me be put to shame.
31.amp: I have stuck [dabaq -- clung fast] unto Your testimonies [eduth]: O LORD [YHWH], put me not to shame [bosh].
31.notes: The dabaq of verse 25 redeemed: the soul that clung to dust now clings to the edut -- the same grip, transferred to the right object. Ruth's cleaving to Naomi is this verb (cf. Ruth 1:14); covenant loyalty is where clinging belongs.

32.text: I will run the way of Your commandments, for You will enlarge my heart.
32.amp: I will run [ruts] the way [derek] of Your commandments [mitsvah], when You shall enlarge [rachab -- widen, set free] my heart [leb].
32.notes: The stanza that began face-down in the dust (v. 25) ends at a sprint: ruts (H7323), running the derek mitsvot. The condition is God's surgery -- rachab (H7337), the heart widened, obedience's lungs enlarged until duty becomes freedom (cf. 2 Corinthians 6:11-13).

33.text: HE. Teach me, O LORD, the way of Your statutes, and I will keep it to the very end.
33.amp: HE. Teach [yarah -- instruct as an archer aims] me, O LORD [YHWH], the way [derek] of Your statutes [choq]; and I shall keep [natsar] it unto the end [eqev -- to the heel, to the last step].
33.notes: The He stanza is eight petitions in a row -- grace begged for every step of obedience. yarah (H3384) is the aiming-teacher's verb, and eqev (H6118), the heel-word: kept to the last footfall of the course.

34.text: Give me understanding, and I will keep Your law -- I will observe it with my whole heart.
34.amp: Give me understanding [bin], and I shall keep [natsar] Your law [torah]; yea, I shall observe [shamar] it with my whole heart [leb].
34.notes: bin (H995) before shamar: the order matters -- understanding is asked as obedience's fuel, and the whole-heart clause returns for the third time. Half-hearted keeping is the one kind this psalm never contemplates.

35.text: Make me tread the path of Your commandments, for that is where my delight lives.
35.amp: Make me to go [darak -- tread] in the path [netibah] of Your commandments [mitsvah]; for therein do I delight [chaphets].
35.notes: darak (H1869), the treading-verb: he asks God to WALK him -- grace supplying the very steps duty requires (cf. Philippians 2:13). The netibah (H5410) is the worn footpath, and chaphets (H2654) confesses the secret: he already loves the road.

36.text: Bend my heart toward Your testimonies, and not toward dishonest gain.
36.amp: Incline [natah -- bend, stretch toward] my heart [leb] unto Your testimonies [eduth], and not to covetousness [betsa -- unjust gain].
36.notes: natah (H5186): the heart as a thing that leans, and only God can re-angle it. The rival is named precisely -- betsa (H1215), profit wrongly got: the pull the edut must outpull in every marketplace generation.

37.text: Make my eyes pass over what is worthless without stopping, and give me life in Your way.
37.amp: Turn away ['make to pass', abar, the KJV margin] my eyes [ayin] from beholding [raah] vanity [shav -- the empty, the worthless]; and quicken [chayah -- revive] me in Your way [derek].
37.notes: abar (H5674): eyes made to pass OVER the shav (H7723) without landing -- the prayer for a disciplined gaze in a world built to catch it. And the alternative to spectating emptiness is chayah, being made alive; dead things entertain, the derek revives.

38.text: Make Your word stand confirmed to Your servant, the word that leads to the fear of You.
38.amp: Stablish [qum -- make stand, confirm] Your word [imrah] unto Your servant [ebed], who is devoted to Your fear [yirah].
38.notes: qum (H6965): the promise asked to stand up and prove itself in the servant's own case. The clause ties promise to reverence -- confirmed imrah (H565) produces yirah (H3374); answered prayer deepens awe, exactly as Psalm 130:4 argued.

39.text: Turn away the reproach that I dread, for Your judgments are good.
39.amp: Turn away [abar] my reproach [cherpah] which I fear [yagor -- dread]: for Your judgments [mishpat] are good [tov].
39.notes: The abar of verse 37 aimed at a second target: the cherpah (H2781) -- perhaps the disgrace his own failure would bring on the Name he carries. The ground of appeal is settled taste: the mishpatim are tov (H2896), and he knows it.

40.text: See how I have longed for Your precepts; in Your righteousness give me life.
40.amp: Behold, I have longed [taab] after Your precepts [piqqudim]: quicken [chayah] me in Your righteousness [tsedaqah].
40.notes: The stanza of petitions rests its case on appetite: taab (H8373), the longing itself presented as evidence. And the He stanza closes on the psalm's heartbeat-request -- chayah (H2421), revive me -- grounded not in his longing but in His tsedaqah.

41.text: WAW. Let Your covenant love come to me, O LORD -- Your salvation, according to Your word --
41.amp: VAU. Let Your mercies [chesed -- covenant love] come [bo] also unto me, O LORD [YHWH], even Your salvation [teshuah], according to Your word [imrah].
41.notes: The Waw stanza (the connecting letter, Hebrew's 'and') links chesed (H2617) to teshuah (H8668): love arriving as rescue, on the schedule the imrah already published. Grace asked for strictly on the basis of what God has said.

42.text: and I will have a word to answer the one who taunts me, for I trust in Your word.
42.amp: So shall I have wherewith to answer [anah] him that reproaches [charaph] me: for I trust [batach] in Your word [dabar].
42.notes: The taunter's question is always the same -- 'where is your God?' (cf. Psalm 42:10) -- and the answer the psalmist wants is a lived one: dabar answered with dabar, the taunt met by testimony. batach (H982), the leaning-trust, supplies the nerve.

43.text: Do not snatch the word of truth utterly out of my mouth, for I have set my hope on Your judgments.
43.amp: And take [natsal -- snatch] not the word [dabar] of truth [emeth] utterly out of my mouth [peh]; for I have hoped [yachal] in Your judgments [mishpat].
43.notes: A strange and honest fear: that failure or silence might empty his mouth of the emeth (H571) it exists to speak. The witness prays to keep his testimony -- and anchors the request in yachal (H3176), hope already staked on the mishpatim.

44.text: Then I will keep Your law without pause, forever and ever;
44.amp: So shall I keep [shamar] Your law [torah] continually [tamid] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
44.notes: Three duration-words stacked -- tamid, olam, ad (H8548, H5769, H5703): obedience with no expiration date contemplated. The vow assumes what the psalm elsewhere begs: a life long enough, and revived enough, to pay it.

45.text: and I will walk in open, roomy freedom, for I have sought Your precepts.
45.amp: And I will walk [halak] at liberty ['at large', rachab, the KJV margin -- in a wide, roomy place]: for I seek [darash] Your precepts [piqqudim].
45.notes: The paradox the world never believes: the sought piqqudim open into rachab (H7342), the broad place -- law experienced as room to run (cf. v. 32). License promises the open field and delivers the pit; the precepts are the actual wide country.

46.text: I will speak of Your testimonies in front of kings and not be put to shame;
46.amp: I will speak [dabar] of Your testimonies [edah] also before kings [melek], and will not be ashamed [bosh].
46.notes: The freed man's range includes thrones: edot spoken before melakim without bosh (H954). Luther took this verse as his motto at Worms; Paul lived it before Agrippa (cf. Acts 26) -- the Word gives its keepers standing in any court.

47.text: and I will take my delight in Your commandments, the commandments I love;
47.amp: And I will delight [shaa] myself in Your commandments [mitsvah], which I have loved [ahab].
47.notes: shaa (H8173) and ahab (H157): delight and love, the affections doing the obeying. Duty has quietly changed categories in this stanza -- from requirement to romance.

48.text: and I will lift up my palms to Your commandments, which I love, and muse deep in Your statutes.
48.amp: My hands [kaph] also will I lift up [nasa] unto Your commandments [mitsvah], which I have loved [ahab]; and I will meditate [siach] in Your statutes [choq].
48.notes: Palms lifted to the mitsvot as in prayer or oath (cf. Psalm 63:4): the body joining the affections -- reaching for the commandments the way hands reach for God. The stanza ends where the psalm lives: siach (H7878), the long musing.

49.text: ZAYIN. Remember the word You gave Your servant, the word on which You made me build my hope.
49.amp: ZAIN. Remember [zakar] the word [dabar] unto Your servant [ebed], upon which You have caused me to hope [yachal].
49.notes: The boldest argument in prayer: reminding God of His own sentence. zakar (H2142) -- and the logic is airtight: YOU caused the hope (yachal, H3176); the expectation is Your handwriting, so honor it.

50.text: This is my comfort in my affliction: that Your word has kept me alive.
50.amp: This is my comfort [nechamah] in my affliction [oni]: for Your word [imrah] has quickened [chayah] me.
50.notes: nechamah (H5165), the comfort-noun, defined by experience: not that affliction lifted but that the imrah kept life in him through it. The verse generations of sufferers have signed their names under.

51.text: The insolent proud have mocked me without measure, yet I have not swerved from Your law.
51.amp: The proud [zed] have had me greatly [meod] in derision [luts -- mocked, scorned]: yet have I not declined [natah -- bent away] from Your law [torah].
51.notes: The zedim (H2086) again, now with luts (H3887), the scorner's laughter at full volume. natah negated: the mocked man's line did not bend -- ridicule being the cheapest and often most effective persecution, resisted here by simple non-swerving.

52.text: I remembered Your judgments from of old, O LORD, and in them I took comfort.
52.amp: I remembered [zakar] Your judgments [mishpat] of old [olam], O LORD [YHWH]; and have comforted [nacham] myself.
52.notes: The counter-move to mockery: zakar me-olam -- memory reaching back down the centuries of God's consistent mishpatim. History is the mocked believer's medicine chest; precedent comforts where argument cannot.

53.text: Burning indignation seizes me because of the wicked who abandon Your law.
53.amp: Horror [zalaphah -- burning indignation] has taken hold [achaz] upon me because of the wicked [rasha] that forsake [azab] Your law [torah].
53.notes: zalaphah (H2152) is a scorching wind of the soul: grief-anger at torah forsaken -- not personal offense but love's response to the Beloved's word trampled. The man who delights most burns most.

54.text: Your statutes have become my songs in the house of my pilgrimage.
54.amp: Your statutes [choq] have been my songs [zemirot] in the house [bayith] of my pilgrimage [magor -- my sojourning].
54.notes: The loveliest line of the stanza: statutes set to music -- zemirot (H2158), the law sung, in the bet magor (H4033), the temporary lodging of a life passing through (cf. v. 19). Pilgrims sing the map they travel by.

55.text: In the night I have remembered Your name, O LORD, and I have kept Your law.
55.amp: I have remembered [zakar] Your name [shem], O LORD [YHWH], in the night [layil], and have kept [shamar] Your law [torah].
55.notes: The third zakar of the stanza, stationed in the layil -- the hours when comfort thins and old fears walk. Night-memory of the shem steadies night-obedience; what fills the sleepless dark shapes the day that follows.

56.text: This has been mine, my own possession: that I have guarded Your precepts.
56.amp: This I had [hayah -- this became mine], because I kept [natsar] Your precepts [piqqudim].
56.notes: The stanza's quiet audit: whatever the proud took with their mocking, 'this' -- the whole treasury of comfort, song, and memory just listed -- became his, by way of natsar (H5341), the guarding. Obedience pays its keepers in kind.

57.text: HETH. My portion is the LORD; I have given my word to keep Your words.
57.amp: CHETH. You are my portion [cheleq], O LORD [YHWH]: I have said [amar] that I would keep [shamar] Your words [dabar].
57.notes: cheleq (H2506), the allotment-word of the land division -- and the Levite's confession, whose portion was the LORD Himself instead of acreage (cf. Numbers 18:20; Psalm 16:5). Content with that estate, the vow follows naturally.

58.text: I have sought the favor of Your face with my whole heart; be gracious to me according to Your word.
58.amp: I intreated [chalah] Your favour ['face', panim, the KJV margin] with my whole heart [leb]: be merciful [chanan -- be gracious] unto me according to Your word [imrah].
58.notes: Literally 'I stroked Your face' -- chalah panim (H2470, H6440), the idiom of earnest entreaty. The whole heart appears a fourth time, and the plea is chanan (H2603): grace, measured by the imrah's own promises.

59.text: I thought hard about my ways, and I turned my feet around to Your testimonies.
59.amp: I thought [chashab -- reckoned, calculated] on my ways [derek], and turned [shub] my feet [regel] unto Your testimonies [edah].
59.notes: Conversion's anatomy in two verbs: chashab (H2803), the honest audit of one's own derek, and shub (H7725), the feet physically re-aimed. Repentance is arithmetic followed by walking -- the prodigal 'came to himself,' then came home (cf. Luke 15:17-20).

60.text: I hurried, and did not linger, to keep Your commandments.
60.amp: I made haste [chush], and delayed [mahah -- lingered, hesitated] not to keep [shamar] Your commandments [mitsvah].
60.notes: chush (H2363) versus mahah (H4102): the two speeds of the will. Delayed obedience quietly plans disobedience; the turned man of verse 59 runs his first steps.

61.text: The ropes of the wicked wrapped around me, but I did not forget Your law.
61.amp: The bands ['companies', chebel, the KJV margin -- the cords, the ropes] of the wicked [rasha] have robbed [ivved -- wrapped, surrounded] me: but I have not forgotten [shakach] Your law [torah].
61.notes: chebel (H2256): either raiding-bands or binding-ropes -- the wicked as entangling cords either way. What they could not confiscate: memory; the torah lives where robbers cannot reach.

62.text: At midnight I rise to give You thanks for the judgments of Your righteousness.
62.amp: At midnight [chatsot layil] I will rise [qum] to give thanks [yadah] unto You because of Your righteous [tsedek] judgments [mishpat].
62.notes: Not insomnia but appointment: qum (H6965) at midnight for deliberate yadah (H3034) -- gratitude worth losing sleep over. Paul and Silas kept this hour in the Philippian stocks (cf. Acts 16:25).

63.text: I am a companion to every man who fears You, to all who keep Your precepts.
63.amp: I am a companion [chaver] of all them that fear [yare] You, and of them that keep [shamar] Your precepts [piqqudim].
63.notes: chaver (H2270), the joined-friend of Ecclesiastes 4:10: the psalmist names his crowd. Fear of God is the membership badge -- one family across every border, class, and century (cf. Psalm 16:3; Malachi 3:16).

64.text: The earth, O LORD, is full of Your covenant love; teach me Your statutes.
64.amp: The earth [eretz], O LORD [YHWH], is full [male] of Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love]: teach [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
64.notes: The stanza closes at planetary scale: eretz male chesed -- the world brim-full of covenant love for eyes trained to see it. And the response to a chesed-flooded earth is the psalm's standing request: lamad, teach me -- learning as the fitting life inside so generous a world.

65.text: TETH. You have dealt well with Your servant, O LORD, just as Your word promised.
65.amp: TETH. You have dealt [asah] well [tov] with Your servant [ebed], O LORD [YHWH], according unto Your word [dabar].
65.notes: The Teth stanza rings the changes on tov, good -- five times in eight verses. The opening entry is testimony, not petition: reviewing the ledger, the servant finds every dealing tov, exactly as the dabar said it would be.

66.text: Teach me good discernment and knowledge, for I have put my faith in Your commandments.
66.amp: Teach [lamad] me good [tov] judgment [taam -- taste, discernment] and knowledge [daat]: for I have believed [aman] Your commandments [mitsvah].
66.notes: taam (H2940) is taste -- the palate of the soul, judgment that can tell good from almost-good. aman (H539) grounds the request: he already believes the mitsvot; he asks now for the trained senses to apply them (cf. Hebrews 5:14).

67.text: Before I was afflicted I was going astray, but now I keep Your word.
67.amp: Before I was afflicted [anah] I went astray [shagag]: but now have I kept [shamar] Your word [imrah].
67.notes: The psalm's famous testimony about pain: the straying (H7683) predated the affliction, and the affliction ended the straying. anah (H6031), the humbling -- God's rumble strip on the road's edge; grief as the grace that turned him back.

68.text: You are good, and You do good; teach me Your statutes.
68.amp: You are good [tov], and do good [tov]; teach [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
68.notes: Five Hebrew words, a complete theology: tov in being, tov in doing -- character and conduct one seamless goodness (cf. Mark 10:18). The response to divine goodness is the psalm's constant appetite: teach me.

69.text: The insolent have plastered me over with a lie, but with my whole heart I will guard Your precepts.
69.amp: The proud [zed] have forged [taphal -- smeared, plastered] a lie [sheqer] against me: but I will keep [natsar] Your precepts [piqqudim] with my whole heart [leb].
69.notes: taphal (H2950): slander as wet plaster troweled over a reputation. The answer is not counter-smear but whole-hearted natsar -- a life kept clean enough, long enough, that the plaster cracks and falls.

70.text: Their heart has grown thick and unfeeling as fat, but I delight in Your law.
70.amp: Their heart [leb] is as fat [taphash -- gross, insensible] as grease [chelev]; but I delight [shaa] in Your law [torah].
70.notes: chelev (H2459), the fat of sacrifices: their leb is larded over, nerve-dead to God (cf. Psalm 17:10; Isaiah 6:10). Against the anesthetized heart, the psalm sets its own vital sign -- shaa, delight: sensitivity to torah as proof of life.

71.text: It was good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn Your statutes.
71.amp: It is good [tov] for me that I have been afflicted [anah]; that I might learn [lamad] Your statutes [choq].
71.notes: Verse 67's testimony promoted to verdict: the affliction itself filed under tov. lamad (H3925) names the tuition pain paid for -- statutes learned in the wards that lectures never taught (cf. Hebrews 12:10-11).

72.text: The law of Your mouth is better to me than thousands in gold and silver.
72.amp: The law [torah] of Your mouth [peh] is better [tov] unto me than thousands [eleph] of gold [zahab] and silver [keseph].
72.notes: The stanza's final tov is an exchange rate: torat pikha -- the law as breath from His own peh -- against alpe zahab va-keseph, thousands in bullion. The afflicted man has run the comparison with real losses on the table, and the Word still wins (cf. Psalm 19:10).

73.text: YODH. Your hands made me and set me firm; give me understanding, that I may learn Your commandments.
73.amp: JOD. Your hands [yad] have made [asah] me and fashioned [kun -- established, formed] me: give me understanding [bin], that I may learn [lamad] Your commandments [mitsvah].
73.notes: The maker's-warranty argument: hands that asah and kun (H3559) the creature can surely finish him with bin (H995). The Word and the workmanship have one Author -- learning His commandments is the built thing reading its Builder's manual (cf. Psalm 139:13-16).

74.text: Those who fear You will see me and be glad, because I have hoped in Your word.
74.amp: They that fear [yare] You will be glad [samach] when they see [raah] me; because I have hoped [yachal] in Your word [dabar].
74.notes: One man's sustained yachal (H3176) becomes the whole fellowship's morale: the God-fearers samach at the sight of hope still standing. Every persevering believer is a public utility.

75.text: I know, O LORD, that Your judgments are righteousness itself, and that in faithfulness You afflicted me.
75.amp: I know [yada], O LORD [YHWH], that Your judgments [mishpat] are right ['righteousness', tsedek, the KJV margin], and that You in faithfulness [emunah] have afflicted [anah] me.
75.notes: The hardest sentence faith learns to say: be-emunah innitani -- in FAITHFULNESS You afflicted me. Not despite the covenant but in keeping of it; the anah of verses 67 and 71 traced to the emunah (H530) behind it.

76.text: Let Your covenant love, I pray, be my comfort, according to Your word to Your servant.
76.amp: Let, I pray, Your merciful kindness [chesed] be for my comfort ['to comfort me', nacham, the KJV margin], according to Your word [imrah] unto Your servant [ebed].
76.notes: Affliction acknowledged as faithful (v. 75) still hurts, so the next breath asks chesed (H2617) as nacham (H5162), comfort -- and cites the file: the imrah made 'to Your servant', promise-comfort with his own name on it.

77.text: Let Your deep compassions come to me, that I may live, for Your law is my delight.
77.amp: Let Your tender mercies [rachamim -- womb-deep compassions] come [bo] unto me, that I may live [chayah]: for Your law [torah] is my delight [shaashuim].
77.notes: rachamim (H7356) arriving so that chayah -- compassion as life-support. The plea's logic: the man whose shaashuim (H8191), whose delight, is the torah has bound his life to its Giver; sustaining him sustains a lover of Your word.

78.text: Let the insolent be shamed, for they wronged me with lies; but I will muse on Your precepts.
78.amp: Let the proud [zed] be ashamed [bosh]; for they dealt perversely [avat -- overthrew me] with me without cause [sheqer -- by falsehood]: but I will meditate [siach] in Your precepts [piqqudim].
78.notes: The imprecation is minimal -- bosh (H954), let their own shame find them -- and the psalmist's energy goes elsewhere: siach (H7878) in the piqqudim. He files the injustice with the Judge and keeps his mind on better matter.

79.text: Let those who fear You turn back to me, those who know Your testimonies.
79.amp: Let those that fear [yare] You turn [shub] unto me, and those that have known [yada] Your testimonies [edah].
79.notes: The slander of verse 69 had apparently scattered his friends; the prayer asks the yare back -- fellowship restored as vindication's sweetest form. The company he wants is defined by what they yada: the edot.

80.text: Let my heart be whole and blameless in Your statutes, so that I am never put to shame.
80.amp: Let my heart [leb] be sound [tamim -- whole, blameless] in Your statutes [choq]; that I be not ashamed [bosh].
80.notes: The stanza closes turning the shame-prayer inward: not 'shame them' but 'keep me unshameable' -- a leb tamim (H8549), whole in the statutes, being the only shame-proofing there is. The tamim of verse 1 asked for by name.

81.text: KAPH. My soul is spent with fainting for Your salvation, but I have hoped in Your word.
81.amp: CAPH. My soul [nephesh] faints [kalah -- is consumed, spent] for Your salvation [teshuah]: but I hope [yachal] in Your word [dabar].
81.notes: The Kaph stanza is the psalm's darkest passage -- kalah (H3615), the being-consumed verb, opens it: a soul burned down to the wick waiting for teshuah (H8668). What remains alight is one thing: yachal in the dabar.

82.text: My eyes are worn out searching for Your word, while I ask, 'When will You comfort me?'
82.amp: My eyes [ayin] fail [kalah] for Your word [imrah], saying [amar], 'When will You comfort [nacham] me?'
82.notes: kalah again, now of the ayin: eyes strained past focus scanning the horizon for the promised imrah. The question is dated faith, not doubt -- 'WHEN will You comfort' assumes the comfort is coming and aches only at the calendar.

83.text: For I have become like a wineskin shriveled in the smoke, yet Your statutes I do not forget.
83.amp: For I am become like a bottle [nod -- a wineskin] in the smoke [qitor]; yet do I not forget [shakach] Your statutes [choq].
83.notes: The nod (H4997) hung above the fire: blackened, cracked, shriveled useless -- the psalmist's self-portrait in affliction. The 'yet' clause is the stanza's spine: memory of the choq outlasting the body's condition.

84.text: How many days does Your servant have left? When will You execute judgment on my pursuers?
84.amp: How many are the days [yom] of Your servant [ebed]? when will You execute [asah] judgment [mishpat] on them that persecute [radaph] me?
84.notes: The mortality question of Psalm 90 turned urgent: the yamim are running out; will vindication arrive inside them? radaph (H7291), the pursuit-verb -- the hunted man asking the Judge to check His docket.

85.text: The insolent have dug pits for me -- men who do not live by Your law.
85.amp: The proud [zed] have dug [karah] pits [shichah] for me, which are not after Your law [torah].
85.notes: karah (H3738), the pit-digging verb of Psalm 7:15: engineered traps, premeditated ruin. The relative clause indicts them precisely -- conduct 'not after Your torah': lawlessness as the pit's true blueprint.

86.text: All Your commandments are faithfulness itself; they pursue me with lies -- help me!
86.amp: All Your commandments [mitsvah] are faithful ['faithfulness', emunah, the KJV margin]: they persecute [radaph] me wrongfully [sheqer -- with falsehood]; help [azar] me.
86.notes: The contrast drawn to a point: kol mitsvot emunah -- utterly reliable -- versus radaph sheqer, pursuit powered by lies. The prayer collapses to two syllables: azreni (H5826), help me -- faith's shortest and most-used sentence.

87.text: They very nearly finished me off on the earth, but I did not forsake Your precepts.
87.amp: They had almost [meat] consumed [kalah] me upon earth [eretz]; but I forsook [azab] not Your precepts [piqqudim].
87.notes: kalah a third time -- the consuming that nearly completed: kimat killuni, they all but ended me. The stanza's arithmetic of survival: everything almost lost on eretz, and the one thing not azab (H5800), not abandoned, was the piqqudim.

88.text: According to Your covenant love, give me life, and I will keep the testimony of Your mouth.
88.amp: Quicken [chayah] me after Your lovingkindness [chesed]; so shall I keep [shamar] the testimony [eduth] of Your mouth [peh].
88.notes: The darkest stanza ends at the psalm's wellhead: chayah (H2421), revive me -- charged now to chesed rather than merit -- and the revived life pre-committed: kept edut, from the same peh that spoke the worlds.

89.text: LAMEDH. Forever, O LORD, Your word stands stationed in the heavens.
89.amp: LAMED. For ever [olam], O LORD [YHWH], Your word [dabar] is settled [natsab -- stands stationed, posted] in heaven [shamayim].
89.notes: After Kaph's smoke, Lamedh opens on granite: le-olam YHWH -- forever, LORD -- devarkha nitsav (H5324), Your word standing posted in the shamayim like a sentinel that cannot be relieved. Everything down here shakes; the original is filed above.

90.text: Your faithfulness runs to generation after generation; You established the earth, and it stands.
90.amp: Your faithfulness [emunah] is unto all generations ['to generation and generation', dor, the KJV margin]: You have established [kun] the earth [eretz], and it abides ['standeth', amad, the KJV margin].
90.notes: emunah le-dor va-dor: the same faithfulness clause as Psalm 100:5, here proven by geology -- the eretz kun (H3559), founded once, still amad (H5975), still standing. The planet under our feet is exhibit A for the reliability of its Maker's word.

91.text: By Your ordinances they stand to this day, for all things are Your servants.
91.amp: They continue [amad -- stand] this day [yom] according to Your ordinances [mishpat]: for all [kol] are Your servants [ebed].
91.notes: The mishpatim here are creation's standing orders -- and the sweeping clause closes it: ha-kol avadekha, ALL things are Your servants. Stars, seasons, and seas wear the same title the psalmist claims; the universe is staff, not sovereign.

92.text: Unless Your law had been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction.
92.amp: Unless [lule] Your law [torah] had been my delights [shaashuim], I should then have perished [abad] in my affliction [oni].
92.notes: The counterfactual every survivor of deep waters recognizes: lule -- had it not been -- torah as shaashuim was the difference between enduring the oni (H6040) and abad (H6), perishing in it. Delight in Scripture as survival equipment, not decoration.

93.text: Never will I forget Your precepts, for through them You have brought me to life.
93.amp: I will never [olam] forget [shakach] Your precepts [piqqudim]: for with them You have quickened [chayah] me.
93.notes: le-olam lo eshkach: forgetting forsworn forever -- and the reason is biographical, not theoretical: bam chiyyitani, by them You revived me. Nobody forgets the rope that pulled him from the pit.

94.text: Yours I am -- save me! For Your precepts have been my search.
94.amp: I am Yours [lekha ani], save [yasha] me; for I have sought [darash] Your precepts [piqqudim].
94.notes: The shortest, strongest plea in the psalm: lekha ani -- Yours I am. Ownership as argument: the Owner protects His property (cf. Isaiah 43:1). The evidence of belonging offered: a life spent in darash of His piqqudim.

95.text: The wicked have waited in ambush to destroy me; I will keep considering Your testimonies.
95.amp: The wicked [rasha] have waited [qavah] for me to destroy [abad] me: but I will consider [bin] Your testimonies [edah].
95.notes: qavah (H6960), the hope-word, chillingly inverted: the resha'im wait for him the way saints wait for God. His counter-tactic is attention management -- bin (H995) fixed on the edot while the ambush idles.

96.text: I have seen the limit of all perfection, but Your commandment is broad beyond measure.
96.amp: I have seen [raah] an end [qets] of all perfection [tiklah]: but Your commandment [mitsvah] is exceeding [meod] broad [rachab].
96.notes: The stanza's summit: everything finished under the sun has a qets (H7093), an edge -- every human excellence surveyed to its boundary line. One thing resisted the survey: the mitsvah, rechabah meod (H7342), wide past measuring -- the same broad country of verses 32 and 45, with no far fence found.

97.text: MEM. Oh how I love Your law! All day long it is my meditation.
97.amp: MEM. O how love I [ahab] Your law [torah]! it is my meditation [sichah] all the day [yom].
97.notes: The psalm's best-known exclamation: mah ahavti toratekha -- love confessed with a gasp, not an argument. sichah (H7881), the all-day musing: the torah as the mind's default screen, what thought returns to when nothing else demands it.

98.text: Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for they are with me forever.
98.amp: You through Your commandments [mitsvah] have made me wiser [chakam] than my enemies [oyeb]: for they are ever ['it is ever with me', olam, the KJV margin] with me.
98.notes: The first of three comparisons: wiser than the oyeb -- because the mitsvah travels with him le-olam, a resident counselor against their visiting cleverness. Wisdom by permanent companionship, not superior talent.

99.text: I carry more insight than all my teachers, for Your testimonies are the matter of my musing.
99.amp: I have more understanding [sakal -- insight, prudence] than all my teachers [lamad]: for Your testimonies [eduth] are my meditation [sichah].
99.notes: Not a student's arrogance but a source-comparison: teachers point at truth; the edot ARE it, and the one who muses (sichah) at the spring outdraws those who lecture downstream. sakal (H7919) is applied insight -- wisdom that works.

100.text: I understand more than the aged, because I have kept Your precepts.
100.amp: I understand [bin] more than the ancients [zaqen -- the elders], because I keep [natsar] Your precepts [piqqudim].
100.notes: The third comparison completes the sweep: enemies, teachers, elders. The zaqen's (H2205) advantage is years; the psalmist's is natsar -- KEPT precepts. Obedience is itself an organ of understanding: the doer knows what the observer only surveys (cf. John 7:17).

101.text: I have held my feet back from every evil path, so that I might keep Your word.
101.amp: I have refrained [kala -- restrained, held back] my feet [regel] from every evil [ra] way [orach], that I might keep [shamar] Your word [dabar].
101.notes: kala (H3607), the restraining-verb: wisdom's negative discipline -- roads deliberately not taken. The purpose clause matters: not abstinence for its own sake but feet kept free FOR the dabar.

102.text: I have not turned aside from Your judgments, for You Yourself have been my Teacher.
102.amp: I have not departed [sur] from Your judgments [mishpat]: for You have taught [yarah] me.
102.notes: The secret of his staying power, stated with the emphatic pronoun: ki-attah horetani -- for YOU taught me. Truth learned from God Himself holds where secondhand instruction slips; the divine Teacher's pupils do not sur (H5493), do not swerve.

103.text: How smooth and sweet are Your words to my palate -- sweeter than honey to my mouth!
103.amp: How sweet [malats -- smooth, pleasant] are Your words [imrah] unto my taste ['palate', chek, the KJV margin]! yea, sweeter than honey [debash] to my mouth [peh]!
103.notes: The taste-test of Psalm 19:10 in the first person: imrah on the chek (H2441), the palate, out-sweetening debash (H1706). Scripture is not merely believed here but tasted -- the affections have a tongue, and it knows what it likes.

104.text: Through Your precepts I gain understanding; therefore I hate every false path.
104.amp: Through Your precepts [piqqudim] I get understanding [bin]: therefore I hate [sane] every false [sheqer] way [orach].
104.notes: The Mem stanza closes with love's necessary shadow: bin gained from the piqqudim produces sane (H8130) toward every orach sheqer. A palate trained on honey recognizes poison; discernment hates accurately.

105.text: NUN. Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light upon my path.
105.amp: NUN. Your word [dabar] is a lamp ['candle', ner, the KJV margin] unto my feet [regel], and a light [or] unto my path [netibah].
105.notes: The most famous verse of the psalm: the ner (H5216), the small clay lamp -- light enough for the next step, not the whole map. The dabar illuminates at walking scale: feet and netibah (H5410), the path underfoot; guidance for travelers, not spectators.

106.text: I have sworn an oath, and I will make it stand: to keep the judgments of Your righteousness.
106.amp: I have sworn [shaba], and I will perform [qum -- make it stand] it, that I will keep [shamar] Your righteous [tsedek] judgments [mishpat].
106.notes: shaba (H7650), the oath-verb: obedience raised to sworn covenant, then qum -- the vow stood upright and kept standing. The lamp of verse 105 shows the road; the oath commits the feet to it.

107.text: I am afflicted beyond measure; give me life, O LORD, according to Your word.
107.amp: I am afflicted [anah] very much [meod]: quicken [chayah] me, O LORD [YHWH], according unto Your word [dabar].
107.notes: The refrain-request at its rawest: naaneti ad-meod, afflicted to the limit -- and the same three-word remedy, chayah according to the dabar. The psalm never pretends the lamp-lit road is smooth; it insists only that the Word revives on it.

108.text: Receive with favor, I pray, the freewill offerings of my mouth, O LORD, and teach me Your judgments.
108.amp: Accept [ratsah], I beseech You, the freewill offerings [nedabah] of my mouth [peh], O LORD [YHWH], and teach [lamad] me Your judgments [mishpat].
108.notes: nedabot pi -- praise as the freewill offering (H5071) of Psalm 110:3, brought from the altar of the mouth. ratsah (H7521) is the priest's acceptance-verb: worship submitted for inspection, with the standing request attached -- teach me.

109.text: My life is in my open hand continually, yet I do not forget Your law.
109.amp: My soul [nephesh] is continually [tamid] in my hand [kaph]: yet do I not forget [shakach] Your law [torah].
109.notes: The idiom of a life carried exposed in the open kaph (H3709) -- one blow from spilling, the fugitive's permanent condition (cf. Judges 12:3; 1 Samuel 19:5). Danger tamid, memory intact: peril does not excuse forgetting; it proves what was truly stored.

110.text: The wicked have set a snare for me, yet I have not strayed from Your precepts.
110.amp: The wicked [rasha] have laid [natan] a snare [pach] for me: yet I erred [taah -- wandered] not from Your precepts [piqqudim].
110.notes: The pach (H6341), the fowler's trap of Psalm 91:3, set squarely on his road -- and the escape is not cleverness but course-keeping: lo taiti, I did not wander. Snares work on the straying; the precept-path runs past them.

111.text: I have taken Your testimonies as my inheritance forever, for they are the joy of my heart.
111.amp: Your testimonies [eduth] have I taken as an heritage [nachal -- taken possession, inherited] for ever [olam]: for they are the rejoicing [sason] of my heart [leb].
111.notes: nachal (H5157), the land-inheritance verb: while others claim acreage, he files his deed on the edot -- an estate no drought or army touches, le-olam. And the property pays income: sason (H8342), heart-joy, the same word Psalm 51:12 begged back.

112.text: I have bent my heart to do Your statutes forever, to the very last step.
112.amp: I have inclined [natah] my heart [leb] to perform ['to do', asah, the KJV margin] Your statutes [choq] alway [olam], even unto the end [eqev -- to the heel].
112.notes: Verse 36 asked God to natah the heart; here the man reports doing it himself -- grace and resolve as one motion, not rivals. The span is total: olam in duration, eqev (H6118) in distance -- forever, and to the last footfall.

113.text: SAMEKH. I hate the half-and-half, the double-minded, but Your law I love.
113.amp: SAMECH. I hate [sane] vain thoughts [seeph -- the divided, the half-hearted]: but Your law [torah] do I love [ahab].
113.notes: seeph (H5588), the divided ones -- men (or thoughts) split between two opinions, Elijah's limpers at Carmel (cf. 1 Kings 18:21) and James's dipsuchos (cf. James 1:8). The stanza's axis is undividedness: sane for the split, ahab for the torah, nothing parked between.

114.text: You are my hiding place and my shield; I put my hope in Your word.
114.amp: You are my hiding place [sether] and my shield [magen]: I hope [yachal] in Your word [dabar].
114.notes: sether (H5643), the covert of Psalm 27:5 and 91:1, paired with the magen (H4043): concealment and defense, the passive and active guards. Between them stands the psalm's constant posture -- yachal, hope staked on the dabar.

115.text: Get away from me, you evildoers, for I will keep the commandments of my God.
115.amp: Depart [sur] from me, ye evildoers [raa]: for I will keep [natsar] the commandments [mitsvah] of my God [Elohim].
115.notes: The one verse in the psalm addressed to the wicked, and it is an eviction notice: suru mimmenni. The undivided man (v. 113) curates his company; the possessive is the ground -- mitsvot ELOHAI, the commandments of MY God.

116.text: Hold me up according to Your word, and I will live; do not let my hope end in shame.
116.amp: Uphold [samak -- support, sustain] me according unto Your word [imrah], that I may live [chayah]: and let me not be ashamed [bosh] of my hope [seber].
116.notes: samak (H5564), the leaning-support of Psalm 51:12: life held up from outside itself. The second clause guards hope's reputation -- let not my seber (H7664), my expectation, be made a public embarrassment; hope in God stakes God's honor on the outcome (cf. Romans 5:5).

117.text: Hold me up, and I will be safe, and I will keep my gaze on Your statutes continually.
117.amp: Hold me up [saad -- sustain, brace], and I shall be safe [yasha]: and I will have respect [shaah -- gaze] unto Your statutes [choq] continually [tamid].
117.notes: saad (H5582), the bracing-verb: salvation as being held. And the held man's occupation: shaah (H8159), the steady gaze at the choq, tamid -- security freeing attention for its true object.

118.text: You have set at nothing all who stray from Your statutes, for their cunning is a lie.
118.amp: You have trodden down [salah -- set at nought, made light of] all them that err [shagah -- stray] from Your statutes [choq]: for their deceit [tarmit] is falsehood [sheqer].
118.notes: salah (H5541): God weighs the strayers and marks them light -- rejected coinage. The verdict's ground: their tarmit (H8649), their cunning, is sheqer at the core; a life built on the false way (v. 104) is appraised at its material's worth.

119.text: All the wicked of the earth You clear away like dross; therefore I love Your testimonies.
119.amp: You put away ['causest to cease', shabat, the KJV margin] all the wicked [rasha] of the earth [eretz] like dross [sig]: therefore I love [ahab] Your testimonies [edah].
119.notes: sig (H5509), the scum the refiner skims off molten silver: judgment as metallurgy, the eretz purified of what never was the metal. The 'therefore' is striking -- God's refining justice makes His edot MORE lovely to the one clinging to them.

120.text: My flesh shudders and stands on end for dread of You, and I am afraid of Your judgments.
120.amp: My flesh [basar] trembles [samar -- bristles, stands on end] for fear [pachad] of You; and I am afraid [yare] of Your judgments [mishpat].
120.notes: samar (H5568): hair-raising awe -- the basar itself responding to God's holiness. The stanza that began with love (v. 113) ends in trembling, and the psalm sees no contradiction: the same Word is honey to the palate and thunder to the flesh.

121.text: AYIN. I have done what is just and righteous; do not abandon me to my oppressors.
121.amp: AIN. I have done [asah] judgment [mishpat] and justice [tsedek]: leave [yanach] me not to mine oppressors [ashaq].
121.notes: The Ayin stanza opens with a clean ledger held up: mishpat and tsedek done -- not sinlessness but covenant integrity in the case at hand. The plea: do not yanach (H3240), do not set me down, into the extortioner's hands.

122.text: Stand as guarantee for Your servant's good; do not let the insolent oppress me.
122.amp: Be surety [arab -- pledge yourself, guarantee] for Your servant [ebed] for good [tov]: let not the proud [zed] oppress [ashaq] me.
122.notes: arab (H6148) is the guarantor's verb -- Judah's word when he pledged himself for Benjamin (cf. Genesis 43:9): the psalmist asks God to co-sign for him. Hebrews answers the prayer with a name: Jesus, the guarantor of a better covenant (cf. Hebrews 7:22).

123.text: My eyes are worn out looking for Your salvation, and for the word of Your righteousness.
123.amp: Mine eyes [ayin] fail [kalah] for Your salvation [yeshuah], and for the word [imrah] of Your righteousness [tsedek].
123.notes: The failing eyes of verse 82 return, fixed now on yeshuah (H3444) -- the salvation whose very name the New Testament will give to a Person. Watching that exhausts the eyes and still keeps watching: hope's endurance test.

124.text: Deal with Your servant according to Your covenant love, and teach me Your statutes.
124.amp: Deal [asah] with Your servant [ebed] according unto Your mercy [chesed], and teach [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
124.notes: The integrity of verse 121 is not the final plea -- chesed (H2617) is: dealt with by covenant love, not by audit. And the request that never rests: lamad, the sixth 'teach me' so far, with more to come.

125.text: Your servant I am; give me understanding, so that I may know Your testimonies.
125.amp: I am Your servant [ebed]; give me understanding [bin], that I may know [yada] Your testimonies [edah].
125.notes: The servant-argument in its simplest form: avdekha ani -- Yours; equip what You own. bin toward yada: understanding sought not for standing but for knowing the Master's edot -- a butler asking to learn the house.

126.text: It is time for the LORD to act: they have torn Your law to pieces.
126.amp: It is time [et] for You, LORD [YHWH], to work [asah]: for they have made void [parar -- broken, annulled] Your law [torah].
126.notes: et laasot la-YHWH: the hour has come for God Himself to act -- prayed when men parar (H6565), annul, the torah wholesale. The verse the reformers loved: when the Word is voided publicly, its Author's intervention becomes the only sufficient answer.

127.text: Therefore I love Your commandments more than gold -- yes, more than the finest gold.
127.amp: Therefore I love [ahab] Your commandments [mitsvah] above gold [zahab]; yea, above fine gold [paz].
127.notes: The 'therefore' hangs on verse 126: precisely BECAUSE the age voids the law, the psalmist raises his valuation -- love above zahab, above paz (H6337), the refined best. Scarcity pricing: the despised Word is the appreciating asset.

128.text: Therefore I count every one of Your precepts concerning all things to be straight and right, and I hate every false path.
128.amp: Therefore I esteem all Your precepts [piqqudim] concerning all things to be right [yashar -- straight]: and I hate [sane] every false [sheqer] way [orach].
128.notes: The stanza's closing audit runs total: KOL piqqudim, concerning KOL things, yashar (H3474) -- the whole counsel declared straight, no clause renegotiated. And the corollary of verse 104 returns as settled policy: every orach sheqer, hated.

129.text: PE. Your testimonies are wonders; therefore my soul guards them.
129.amp: PE. Your testimonies [eduth] are wonderful [pele -- wonders, marvels]: therefore does my soul [nephesh] keep [natsar] them.
129.notes: pele (H6382) is the miracle-word -- the category of the Red Sea applied to the written edot: Scripture itself classed among God's wonders. The logic is a collector's: the nephesh guards what it knows to be priceless.

130.text: The opening up of Your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.
130.amp: The entrance [pethach -- the opening, the doorway] of Your words [dabar] gives light [or]; it gives understanding [bin] unto the simple [peti].
130.notes: pethach (H6608): the words as a door that lights the room the moment it opens -- unfolding Scripture as sunrise. And the light is democratic: the peti (H6612), the unschooled and open, walk out with bin that academies cannot confer (cf. Psalm 19:7).

131.text: I opened my mouth wide and panted, for I was longing for Your commandments.
131.amp: I opened [paar -- opened wide] my mouth [peh], and panted [shaaph -- gasped]: for I longed [yaab] for Your commandments [mitsvah].
131.notes: shaaph (H7602), the panting of Ecclesiastes' sun and Psalm 42's deer: appetite for the mitsvot at the level of air-hunger. yaab (H2968) occurs only here in all Scripture -- a longing that needed its own word.

132.text: Turn Your face to me and be gracious to me, as You always do for those who love Your name.
132.amp: Look [panah -- turn, face toward] upon me, and be merciful [chanan -- be gracious] unto me, as You use to do ['according to the custom toward', mishpat, the KJV margin] unto those that love [ahab] Your name [shem].
132.notes: The lovely legal idiom: ke-mishpat -- 'according to the custom' -- God's habitual dealing with Name-lovers cited as precedent. The psalmist asks for the house policy: the panah and chanan (H6437, H2603) that the ohabe shem have always received.

133.text: Make my footsteps firm in Your word, and let no iniquity get dominion over me.
133.amp: Order [kun -- establish, make firm] my steps [paam] in Your word [imrah]: and let not any iniquity [aven] have dominion [shalat] over me.
133.notes: kun (H3559) applied at footstep resolution: each paam (H6471) set in the imrah like stones in mortar. The second clause knows sin's ambition -- aven (H205) seeks shalat, ruling power (cf. Genesis 4:7; Romans 6:14); the ordered walk is the coup prevention.

134.text: Ransom me from the oppression of man, and I will keep Your precepts.
134.amp: Deliver [padah -- ransom, redeem] me from the oppression [osheq] of man [adam]: so will I keep [shamar] Your precepts [piqqudim].
134.notes: padah (H6299), the ransom-verb of Psalm 130:8: bought out from under the osheq (H6233) of adam -- human systems of extortion and pressure. Freedom's stated purpose, as always in this psalm: room to shamar.

135.text: Let Your face shine down on Your servant, and teach me Your statutes.
135.amp: Make Your face [panim] to shine [or] upon Your servant [ebed]; and teach [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
135.notes: The Aaronic blessing prayed in the first person (cf. Numbers 6:25): panekha haer -- the shining face, favor as light. And in its warmth, the psalm's inextinguishable request rises once more: lamad, teach me.

136.text: Channels of water run down from my eyes, because men will not keep Your law.
136.amp: Rivers [peleg] of waters [mayim] run down [yarad] mine eyes [ayin], because they keep [shamar] not Your law [torah].
136.notes: peleg (H6388), the irrigation-channels of Psalm 1:3, here cut by grief down a face: weeping at torah trampled -- not at personal loss. The Pe stanza ends where Jeremiah's and Jesus' tears fall (cf. Jeremiah 9:1; Luke 19:41): love for God weeping over lawless men.

137.text: TSADHE. You are righteous, O LORD, and Your judgments are upright.
137.amp: TZADDI. Righteous [tsaddiq] are You, O LORD [YHWH], and upright [yashar] are Your judgments [mishpat].
137.notes: The Tsadhe stanza plays on its own letter: tsaddiq, tsedek, tsedaqah chime through all eight verses. The order of the confession matters -- He is tsaddiq (H6662) first, and the mishpatim are yashar (H3477) because of who issues them.

138.text: The testimonies You have commanded are righteousness itself, and faithfulness through and through.
138.amp: Your testimonies [edah] that You have commanded [tsavah] are righteous ['righteousness', tsedek, the KJV margin] and very [meod] faithful ['faithfulness', emunah, the KJV margin].
138.notes: The Hebrew uses nouns, not adjectives: the edot ARE tsedek, ARE emunah meod -- righteousness and faithfulness in written form. Scripture does not merely describe these qualities; it instantiates them.

139.text: My zeal has eaten me up, because my adversaries have forgotten Your words.
139.amp: My zeal [qinah] has consumed ['cut me off', tsamat, the KJV margin] me, because mine enemies [tsar] have forgotten [shakach] Your words [dabar].
139.notes: qinah (H7068), the jealousy-zeal that consumed the Messiah at the temple (cf. Psalm 69:9; John 2:17): the psalmist burns not at being wronged but at the dabar shakach -- the words forgotten. The gravest offense in his ledger is amnesia toward God.

140.text: Your word is refined through and through, tested in the furnace, and Your servant loves it.
140.amp: Your word [imrah] is very [meod] pure ['tried, refined', tsaraph, the KJV margin]: therefore Your servant [ebed] loves [ahab] it.
140.notes: tsaraph (H6884), the smelter's verb: the imrah as metal that has been through the fire meod -- every promise assayed by centuries of testing, zero dross found (cf. Psalm 12:6; Proverbs 30:5). Love resting on metallurgy: the ebed loves what has been proven.

141.text: Small am I, and despised, yet Your precepts I do not forget.
141.amp: I am small [tsair -- young, insignificant] and despised [bazah]: yet do not I forget [shakach] Your precepts [piqqudim].
141.notes: tsair (H6810): little in the world's ranking, bazah (H959) in its regard -- and the 'yet' clause holds the line the enemies dropped in verse 139: THEY forgot the words; the small man does not. Faithfulness is not sized by standing.

142.text: Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and Your law is truth itself.
142.amp: Your righteousness [tsedaqah] is an everlasting [olam] righteousness [tsedek], and Your law [torah] is the truth [emeth].
142.notes: The stanza's letter-words at full stack: tsedaqah that is tsedek olam -- righteousness with no expiration -- and the flat equation Jesus prayed to the Father: torah emeth, Your word is truth (cf. John 17:17).

143.text: Trouble and anguish have found me and taken hold, yet Your commandments are my delight.
143.amp: Trouble [tsar] and anguish [matsoq] have taken hold ['found me', matsa, the KJV margin] on me: yet Your commandments [mitsvah] are my delights [shaashuim].
143.notes: tsar and matsoq (H6862, H4689): the narrowing words -- distress as a closing corridor. Inside it, the mitsvot remain shaashuim (H8191), delights: joy in the Word is pressure-rated, and this verse is its certification.

144.text: The righteousness of Your testimonies is everlasting; give me understanding, and I will live.
144.amp: The righteousness [tsedek] of Your testimonies [eduth] is everlasting [olam]: give me understanding [bin], and I shall live [chayah].
144.notes: The stanza closes joining its two threads: tsedek olam, the everlasting rightness -- and the psalm's life-verb chayah, keyed here to bin: understanding as oxygen. To understand the eternal testimonies is to breathe.

145.text: QOPH. I cried out with my whole heart: answer me, O LORD! I will keep Your statutes.
145.amp: KOPH. I cried [qara] with my whole heart [leb]; hear [anah -- answer] me, O LORD [YHWH]: I will keep [natsar] Your statutes [choq].
145.notes: The Qoph stanza is the psalm's prayer-clinic: qara (H7121) with kol leb -- the whole-heart formula's final appearances -- and the vow riding on the request. Wanting an answer and intending obedience arrive in the same breath.

146.text: I cried out to You: save me, and I will keep Your testimonies.
146.amp: I cried [qara] unto You; save [yasha] me, and I shall keep ['that I may keep', shamar, the KJV margin] Your testimonies [edah].
146.notes: The margin reading gives salvation its purpose clause: hoshieni ve-eshmerah -- save me THAT I may keep. Rescue is asked as enablement: the saved life's job description is already drafted.

147.text: I rose before the dawn itself and cried for help; I have put my hope in Your word.
147.amp: I prevented [qadam -- came before, forestalled] the dawning of the morning [nesheph -- the twilight], and cried [shava]: I hoped [yachal] in Your word [dabar].
147.notes: qadam (H6923): the psalmist beats the sun to its post -- up before the nesheph (H5399), the last dark before day, already crying shava (H7768). Hope in the dabar sets alarm clocks.

148.text: My eyes stayed open ahead of every night watch, to muse on Your word.
148.amp: Mine eyes [ayin] prevent [qadam] the night watches [ashmurah], that I might meditate [siach] in Your word [imrah].
148.notes: The other end of the clock: qadam again, now of the ashmurot (H821), the night watches of Psalm 90:4 -- eyes open before each one, siach in the imrah while the city sleeps. Dawn and midnight both annexed for meditation.

149.text: Hear my voice according to Your covenant love; O LORD, give me life according to Your judgment.
149.amp: Hear [shama] my voice [qol] according unto Your lovingkindness [chesed]: O LORD [YHWH], quicken [chayah] me according to Your judgment [mishpat].
149.notes: Two 'according-to' clauses in one breath: heard by the measure of chesed, revived by the measure of mishpat -- love and justice as the same request's two warrants. The chayah refrain sounds again; it will toll to the psalm's end.

150.text: Those who chase after wicked schemes are drawing close; they are far away from Your law.
150.amp: They draw nigh [qarav] that follow [radaph] after mischief [zimmah -- the wicked scheme]: they are far [rachaq] from Your law [torah].
150.notes: The verse maps two distances at once: the schemers qarav (H7126), closing in physically -- while rachaq (H7368), far, from the torah morally. Proximity to the psalmist, distance from God: the geometry of every persecution.

151.text: But You, O LORD, are near at hand, and every commandment of Yours is truth.
151.amp: You are near [qarov], O LORD [YHWH]; and all Your commandments [mitsvah] are truth [emeth].
151.notes: The answer to verse 150 in its own vocabulary: qarov attah YHWH -- nearer than the nearing enemies (cf. Psalm 34:18; 145:18). And with Him, the mitsvot: kol emeth, all truth -- company and certainty in the same room.

152.text: Long ago I learned from Your testimonies that You founded them to stand forever.
152.amp: Concerning Your testimonies [edah], I have known [yada] of old [qedem] that You have founded [yasad] them for ever [olam].
152.notes: The Qoph stanza closes on bedrock: qedem (H6924), knowledge dating back years -- the edot yasad (H3245), foundation-laid, le-olam. He has tested them long enough to certify the engineering: they were built to outlast everything now threatening him.

153.text: RESH. Look upon my affliction and pull me out, for I have not forgotten Your law.
153.amp: RESH. Consider [raah -- see] mine affliction [oni], and deliver [chalats -- draw me out] me: for I do not forget [shakach] Your law [torah].
153.notes: The Resh stanza runs on the seeing-verb raah: three times the psalmist asks God to LOOK. chalats (H2502) is the drawing-out rescue of Psalm 34:7 -- and the plea's credential is the psalm's constant one: memory that held.

154.text: Plead my case and redeem me as my Kinsman; give me life according to Your word.
154.amp: Plead [rib] my cause [rib], and deliver [gaal -- redeem as Kinsman-Redeemer] me: quicken [chayah] me according to Your word [imrah].
154.notes: Three offices asked of One Person: advocate (rib, H7378 -- take my lawsuit), goel (H1350 -- the kinsman who buys back), and life-giver. The triple office has a New Testament name in each case (cf. 1 John 2:1; Galatians 3:13; John 11:25).

155.text: Salvation stands far off from the wicked, for they do not seek Your statutes.
155.amp: Salvation [yeshuah] is far [rachoq] from the wicked [rasha]: for they seek [darash] not Your statutes [choq].
155.notes: The far-and-near geometry concluded: yeshuah rachoq from the resha'im -- not because grace has a fence but because they do not darash (H1875); salvation is distant from those walking the other way. The seeking psalm states its converse once, plainly.

156.text: Great and many are Your tender compassions, O LORD; give me life according to Your judgments.
156.amp: Great ['many', rav, the KJV margin] are Your tender mercies [rachamim], O LORD [YHWH]: quicken [chayah] me according to Your judgments [mishpat].
156.notes: rachamim rabbim (H7356, H7227): compassions both deep and NUMEROUS -- a plural noun counted in the plural. The chayah refrain draws on that stock: one revival per compassion would outlast any affliction.

157.text: Many are my persecutors and my adversaries, yet I have not bent away from Your testimonies.
157.amp: Many [rav] are my persecutors [radaph] and mine enemies [tsar]; yet do I not decline [natah -- bend away] from Your testimonies [eduth].
157.notes: The same counting-word as verse 156 -- rav -- now tallying the radaph and tsar: compassions many, persecutors many, and the man between them unbent (natah, H5186, negated). The arithmetic of endurance: His mercies outnumber their spears.

158.text: I looked on the treacherous and was filled with loathing, because they do not keep Your word.
158.amp: I beheld [raah] the transgressors [bagad -- the treacherous, the faithless], and was grieved [qut -- filled with loathing]; because they kept [shamar] not Your word [imrah].
158.notes: bagad (H898) is covenant-treachery -- faithlessness to sworn bonds. qut (H6962), the grief-loathing of Psalm 139:21: what turns his stomach is not their success but the imrah unkept; love for the Word calibrates all his revulsions.

159.text: See how I have loved Your precepts; O LORD, give me life according to Your covenant love.
159.amp: Consider [raah] how I love [ahab] Your precepts [piqqudim]: quicken [chayah] me, O LORD [YHWH], according to Your lovingkindness [chesed].
159.notes: The third raah of the stanza: look at my affliction (v. 153), at the treacherous (v. 158), and now at this -- ahab for the piqqudim, the one exhibit the psalmist dares present. Yet the revival is asked per His chesed, not per the exhibit: love appeals to greater Love.

160.text: The sum of Your word is truth, and every judgment of Your righteousness endures forever.
160.amp: Your word [dabar] is true ['the beginning of thy word is true', rosh, the KJV margin] from the beginning [rosh -- the head, the sum]: and every one of Your righteous [tsedek] judgments [mishpat] endures for ever [olam].
160.notes: rosh debarkha emeth: the head, the sum-total, of Your word is truth -- Scripture true in aggregate and in each mishpat singly, le-olam. The Resh stanza ends by auditing the whole book and certifying every line.

161.text: SHIN. Princes have persecuted me for no reason at all, but my heart stands in awe only of Your word.
161.amp: SCHIN. Princes [sar] have persecuted [radaph] me without a cause [chinnam -- gratuitously, for nothing]: but my heart [leb] stands in awe [pachad -- trembles] of Your word [dabar].
161.notes: chinnam (H2600): persecution with no invoice attached -- the word Jesus applied to His own case, 'they hated Me without cause' (cf. John 15:25; Psalm 69:4). The heart's economy is the point: sarim could not make it pachad (H6342); only the dabar commands that trembling.

162.text: I rejoice over Your word like a man who has found great plunder.
162.amp: I rejoice [sus] at Your word [imrah], as one that finds [matsa] great [rav] spoil [shalal -- plunder, battle-spoil].
162.notes: shalal (H7998): the victor's haul after battle -- wealth suddenly, entirely, undeservedly yours. Every fresh finding (matsa, H4672) in the imrah lands like that: the reader as a soldier stumbling into the enemy's abandoned treasury.

163.text: Falsehood I hate and abhor; Your law is what I love.
163.amp: I hate [sane] and abhor [taab -- detest as abominable] lying [sheqer]: but Your law [torah] do I love [ahab].
163.notes: The psalm's affections at full contrast in one line: sane and taab (H8581) stacked against sheqer, ahab reserved for torah. Neutrality toward falsehood is the one position the verse leaves no room for.

164.text: Seven times a day I praise You for the judgments of Your righteousness.
164.amp: Seven times [sheba] a day [yom] do I praise [halal] You because of Your righteous [tsedek] judgments [mishpat].
164.notes: sheba (H7651), the completeness-number: praise punctuating the whole day at every watch -- the verse behind the church's seven daily offices. Not a quota but a fullness: gratitude structured into the clock itself.

165.text: Great peace belongs to those who love Your law, and no stumbling block can bring them down.
165.amp: Great [rav] peace [shalom] have they which love [ahab] Your law [torah]: and nothing shall offend them ['they shall have no stumblingblock', mikshol, the KJV margin].
165.notes: shalom rav (H7965, H7227): peace in bulk, deeded to the torah-lovers. The mikshol (H4383) is the stumbling block -- and the promise is not a cleared road but a sure-footed walker: what trips the world does not fell those whose footing is the Word (cf. 1 John 2:10).

166.text: I have hoped for Your salvation, O LORD, and I have done Your commandments.
166.amp: LORD [YHWH], I have hoped [sabar -- waited expectantly] for Your salvation [yeshuah], and done [asah] Your commandments [mitsvah].
166.notes: The verse old Simeon lived into flesh -- 'waiting for the consolation of Israel' until he held the yeshuah (H3444) in his arms (cf. Luke 2:25-30). Hope and obedience in one sentence: sabar (H7663) looking forward, asah working meanwhile.

167.text: My soul has kept Your testimonies, and I love them exceedingly.
167.amp: My soul [nephesh] has kept [shamar] Your testimonies [edah]; and I love [ahab] them exceedingly [meod].
167.notes: The keeping is credited to the nephesh itself -- obedience from the core, not the surface -- and the motive files right behind it: ahab meod (H3966), love at full strength. The psalm's two great verbs, kept and loved, finally side by side.

168.text: I have kept Your precepts and Your testimonies, for all my ways are open before You.
168.amp: I have kept [shamar] Your precepts [piqqudim] and Your testimonies [edah]: for all my ways [derek] are before You.
168.notes: The Shin stanza closes with the psalm's deepest motive for integrity: kol derakhai negdekha -- every way of mine lies open before You. Obedience as life lived facing the Watcher of Psalm 139: nothing performed, nothing hidden.
