169.text: TAW. Let my ringing cry come near, right up before Your face, O LORD; give me understanding according to Your word.
169.amp: TAU. Let my cry [rinnah -- ringing cry] come near [qarav] before [panim] You, O LORD [YHWH]: give me understanding [bin] according to Your word [dabar].
169.notes: The last stanza opens with prayer asking for clearance: the rinnah (H7440) brought qarav, near, into the panim. And after 168 verses, the request is still the first one: bin, understanding -- the student's appetite undiminished at the course's end.

170.text: Let my plea for grace come before You; rescue me according to Your word.
170.amp: Let my supplication [techinnah -- plea for favor] come [bo] before [panim] You: deliver [natsal] me according to Your word [imrah].
170.notes: techinnah (H8467), the grace-plea built on chanan: petition that argues no merit, twinned with verse 169's cry. Both ride the same rail into the presence -- 'according to Your word', the psalm's address on every envelope.

171.text: My lips will pour out praise like a bubbling spring, for You teach me Your statutes.
171.amp: My lips [saphah] shall utter [naba -- bubble up, pour forth] praise [tehillah], when You have taught [lamad] me Your statutes [choq].
171.notes: naba (H5042), the gushing-spring verb of Psalm 19:2: praise under pressure, overflowing rather than pumped. The cause is the psalm's answered request -- lamad, the teaching finally received becomes tehillah on the way out.

172.text: Let my tongue sing back Your word in answer, for all Your commandments are righteousness.
172.amp: My tongue [lashon] shall speak [anah -- answer, sing back] of Your word [imrah]: for all [kol] Your commandments [mitsvah] are righteousness [tsedek].
172.notes: anah (H6030) is to answer or sing antiphonally: the tongue responding to the imrah like a choir's second line -- Scripture as the first voice, testimony as the reply. The ground: kol mitsvot tsedek, the whole canon righteous, nothing to skip in the singing.

173.text: Let Your hand stand ready to help me, for Your precepts are what I have chosen.
173.amp: Let Your hand [yad] help [azar] me; for I have chosen [bachar] Your precepts [piqqudim].
173.notes: bachar (H977), the election-verb of verse 30: the psalmist chose the piqqudim, and now asks the Hand that wrote them to back the choice. Commitment calls in its covenant support -- the chooser is never left to fund the choice alone.

174.text: I have longed for Your salvation, O LORD, and Your law is my delight.
174.amp: I have longed [taab] for Your salvation [yeshuah], O LORD [YHWH]; and Your law [torah] is my delight [shaashuim].
174.notes: The longing-verb of verse 40 aimed at its final object: yeshuah -- the salvation whose Hebrew name became Yeshua. Meanwhile the torah remains shaashuim (H8191), the delight that makes the waiting sweet: longing and delighting, the believer's two simultaneous tenses.

175.text: Let my soul live, and it will praise You; and let Your judgments come to my help.
175.amp: Let my soul [nephesh] live [chayah], and it shall praise [halal] You; and let Your judgments [mishpat] help [azar] me.
175.notes: The chayah refrain's final toll, with its purpose clause attached: tehi nafshi u-tehallelekha -- let the soul live AND IT WILL PRAISE. Life is asked for as choir recruitment; even the mishpatim are enlisted as helpers on the way.

176.text: I have wandered off like a lost sheep. Seek Your servant, for I have not forgotten Your commandments.
176.amp: I have gone astray [taah -- wandered] like a lost [abad -- perishing] sheep [seh]; seek [baqash] Your servant [ebed]; for I do not forget [shakach] Your commandments [mitsvah].
176.notes: The great psalm's stunning last word: after 175 verses of loving, keeping, and vowing -- taiti ke-seh obed, I have strayed like a perishing sheep. The final prayer is not 'I will find my way' but baqesh avdekha, SEEK Your servant: the whole psalm rests at last on the Shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine (cf. Isaiah 53:6; Luke 15:4-5). And the last clause holds the thread: the commandments, not forgotten -- a lost sheep that still knows its Master's voice.
